If you replace every plank of a ship, is it still the same ship?
It's the Ship of Theseus, a puzzle the Greek writer Plutarch recorded about two thousand years ago.
Athenians kept the hero's ship for generations, swapping each rotting plank for a fresh one.
Eventually, not one original plank remained. So was it still his ship?
Now it gets worse. Suppose someone gathers every old plank and rebuilds the ship.
Now there are two. One has the original parts. The other has the original history.
Philosophers split. Some say identity lives in the matter. Others say it lives in the continuous form.
You're the same puzzle. Many of your body's cells are replaced over the years, yet you feel like one person.
Maybe “same” isn't a fact the universe hands us. Maybe it's a line we choose to draw.
